layers.name: Oceans & seas
layers.description: Named marine geography that gives the political map a readable physical frame.

provenance.methodology: Natural Earth 1:10m marine-area polygons are bounded to globally and regionally meaningful named waters at source scale rank 4 or better. Coastline adjacency is derived from generalized geometry and never asserts ownership or jurisdiction.
authoredVisualChoices: Marine areas use restrained transparent blue ink and a dedicated label hierarchy. The selection is deliberately bounded rather than an exhaustive gazetteer.

layers.name: Drainage basins
layers.description: Generalized basin extents for five major river systems.

provenance.methodology: Five reviewed World Bank major-river-basin polygons are rendered as generalized learning extents. They are not engineering, legal, or local watershed boundaries.
authoredVisualChoices: A translucent amber wash and dashed boundary distinguish basin area from river centerlines without implying political ownership or control.

layers.name: Political
layers.description: Countries and territories differentiated for geographic exploration.

provenance.methodology: Each country has a stable color chosen for this Atlas. Color does not indicate a measured value, alliance or recognition of a territorial claim.
authoredVisualChoices: France and the United States are blue; the United Kingdom is rose, China red and Mexico green. Supporting country colors are explicitly recorded in the versioned JJU palette.

layers.name: Government
layers.description: Broad current government form, with original source wording retained for each place.

provenance.methodology: Rule-based normalization of retained source wording into broad, revisable categories.
authoredVisualChoices: Broad categories trade institutional nuance for legibility at world scale.

layers.name: Religion
layers.description: Dominant broad tradition. Country details retain composition and estimate year.

provenance.methodology: Broad-tradition shares are normalized only where source wording supports a defensible comparison.
authoredVisualChoices: The default displays dominant broad tradition; it does not claim denominations are interchangeable or equally measured.

layers.name: Population
layers.description: Population intensity using the latest World Bank observation in this snapshot.

provenance.methodology: Uses the latest available World Bank observation per economy without rewriting its year.
authoredVisualChoices: Country totals are binned for world-scale legibility and are not population density.

layers.name: GDP per capita
layers.description: Economic output per person in current US dollars, using each economy's latest available World Bank observation.

provenance.methodology: Uses NY.GDP.PCAP.CD and retains each economy's actual observation year. No inflation or purchasing-power adjustment is implied.
authoredVisualChoices: A logarithmic scale makes world-scale differences visible without letting a few extreme values erase the rest.
The fixed domain and five-stop palette are authored display choices, not properties of the source data.

layers.name: Urban population share
layers.description: The share of people living in nationally defined urban areas.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS and retains each economy's observation year. Urban definitions come from national statistical offices and are not perfectly harmonized.
authoredVisualChoices: The fixed 0–100% linear scale supports direct percentage comparison; color does not imply city quality or development.

layers.name: Population growth
layers.description: Annual population change, including births, deaths and migration.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.POP.GROW, the exponential annual rate of change in de facto midyear population, retaining each economy's observation year.
authoredVisualChoices: A diverging scale centers zero so decline and growth read as different directions; visual clamping at ±5% does not alter tooltip values.

layers.name: Children and young teens
layers.description: The share of the population ages 0–14.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.POP.0014.TO.ZS as a share of de facto total population and retains each economy's observation year.
authoredVisualChoices: A fixed 0–50% scale makes countries comparable without recalculating colors from the current snapshot.

layers.name: Older population
layers.description: The share of the population ages 65 and above.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS as a share of de facto total population and retains each economy's observation year.
authoredVisualChoices: A fixed 0–40% scale reveals global age-structure differences while retaining outlier values in tooltips.

layers.name: Fertility rate
layers.description: The period total fertility rate, measured as births per woman.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.DYN.TFRT.IN, a period rate implied by the age-specific fertility rates of the stated year, and retains each economy's observation year.
authoredVisualChoices: The fixed linear scale shows the full observed world range; it does not label demographic outcomes as good or bad.

layers.name: Life expectancy
layers.description: Period life expectancy at birth under the mortality pattern of the observation year.

provenance.methodology: Uses SP.DYN.LE00.IN as period life expectancy at birth and retains each economy's observation year; it is not an individual lifespan forecast.
authoredVisualChoices: The fixed 50–90 year linear scale emphasizes meaningful world differences while preserving exact values in tooltips.

layers.name: Modern borders
layers.description: Present-day Atlas entity boundaries, kept independent from thematic fills.

provenance.methodology: Derived Mercator paths preserve the canonical Natural Earth entity join. Mercator preserves local angles, not area; high-latitude countries appear disproportionately large.
authoredVisualChoices: Boundary weight is a renderer choice and does not encode legal certainty.

layers.name: Country interaction targets
layers.description: Transparent hit targets so selection behavior does not depend on a visual layer.

provenance.methodology: Interaction targets use the same joined geometry as visible entity paths and tiny-territory markers.
authoredVisualChoices: The hit layer is intentionally independent of fill, boundary, and annotation rendering.

layers.name: Physical relief
layers.description: Source-derived terrain relief, with regional detail loaded as you zoom.

provenance.methodology: Natural Earth manual shaded relief is bilinearly reprojected from its original 10800 × 5400 WGS84 image to the registered Mercator viewBox. A viewport-loaded detail level retains source structure instead of enlarging the world overview. Direct grayscale, with no contrast amplification or synthetic terrain.
authoredVisualChoices: 34% multiply in Political and Where People Live; 18% in national analytical views to protect the thematic color hierarchy. Opacity is a authored visual choice, not an elevation measurement.
The original 1/30-degree pixels are approximately 3.7 km at the equator; projected display resolution is not additional geographic accuracy.

layers.name: Population density
layers.description: Modelled people per square kilometre in the 2025 GHSL epoch.

provenance.methodology: The GHSL R2023A modelled 2025 population-count grid is area-resampled from one-kilometre World Mollweide cells into an overview and three tiled detail levels matching the Mercator vector projection. Zoom loads source-derived regional, country and close detail, not an enlargement of the overview. Projected pixels do not imply finer original observations.
authoredVisualChoices: The color and alpha ramp uses log1p scaling so sparse settlement and metropolitan concentrations can coexist legibly.
Transparent zeroes expose the physical base; a display pixel averages many source cells and is not an exact cell reading.

layers.name: Major lakes
layers.description: Selected Natural Earth lakes with canonical WGS84 geometry and a Mercator derivative.

provenance.methodology: Natural Earth 1:50m geometry at overview scales, replaced with 1:10m geometry as you zoom. Geographic detail remains generalized; it is not a navigational survey.
authoredVisualChoices: Only generalized major lakes appear at world scale; absence does not mean a place has no lakes.

layers.name: Major rivers
layers.description: Selected Natural Earth river centerlines with canonical WGS84 geometry and a Mercator derivative.

provenance.methodology: Natural Earth 1:50m geometry at overview scales, replaced with 1:10m geometry as you zoom. Geographic detail remains generalized; it is not a navigational survey.
authoredVisualChoices: World-scale river selection expands progressively with source 1:10m river branches at closer zoom. Blue screen-width ink stays independent of camera scale; this is not a complete drainage survey.

layers.name: Major cities
layers.description: National capitals and selected high-priority populated places.

provenance.methodology: Natural Earth 1:10m populated places. Symbols identify cities; size is a reading hierarchy, not a population measure. Labels and selectable targets appear progressively.
authoredVisualChoices: City symbols indicate selected settlements, not exact comparable metropolitan populations; Natural Earth cartographic rank and capital status control their size.

layers.name: Contextual explanations
layers.description: Optional source-reviewed notes that explain conspicuous patterns without covering the map in prose.

provenance.methodology: Each note is tied to explicit geography, the rendered population observation, supporting evidence, source dates, caveats, and a review status in pattern-notes.v1.json.
authoredVisualChoices: Only four strong, visually prompted explanations are included; markers remain subtle and the internal PatternNote model name is not exposed as permanent product language.

viewPresets.description: The share of people living in areas each country defines as urban. Definitions differ across countries.

viewPresets.name: Population growth
viewPresets.description: Annual population change from births, deaths and migration—not fertility alone.

viewPresets.question: Where do children and young teens make up the largest share of society?

viewPresets.name: Older population
viewPresets.description: The share of each population ages 65 and above.
viewPresets.question: Where do older adults make up the largest share of society?

viewPresets.name: Fertility
viewPresets.description: The period total fertility rate implied by the observation year's age-specific rates.
viewPresets.question: Where are present fertility rates highest and lowest?

viewPresets.description: Period life expectancy at birth under the mortality pattern of the observation year.
